explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates VELA (their proposed LLM-hybrid-as-a-judge approach) against human evaluation by comparing both methods on the same test sets (TestA and TestB) using Kendall's tau correlation metrics, reporting quantitative results for each evaluation criterion

prompts.notes: Full prompts for Descriptiveness, Relevance, and Fluency provided in Appendix J.1, J.2, and J.3 respectively, including detailed scoring rubrics from 1-5

guidelines.notes: Detailed scoring guidelines for Descriptiveness, Relevance, and Fluency provided in Appendix K, with 5-point scale definitions and evaluation criteria

sample_size.notes: TestA has 294 samples, TestB has 324 samples (total 618 samples). Each candidate was evaluated by minimum 3 annotators. Results shown separately for TestA and TestB sets

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Direct comparison to human performance scores

validation_results.summary_finding: VELA achieved superhuman performance on LongCap-Arena, outperforming human evaluation in Descriptiveness (TestA: 56.4 vs 55.1, TestB: 54.0 vs 48.7) and Fluency (TestA: 57.4 vs 28.1, TestB: 39.0 vs 23.4), while slightly underperforming in Relevance on TestA (40.0 vs 41.0)

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-as-a-judge and human evaluation used identical three criteria: Descriptiveness, Relevance, and Fluency, with the same 5-point scale definitions
